I farm the same 8 mu in wheat-maize rotation, so I will run all 8 mu through wheat and then all 8 mu through maize. I do not like changing too much unless I see it work nearby, so this year I will mostly follow what has been giving steady harvests around me. For wheat, I will use the same kind of improved seed that the better-yielding families around here plant, not old saved seed. Wheat is where I do not want to be stingy, because if the stand is weak after winter, it is hard to fix later. I will put enough base fertilizer on before sowing, then topdress nitrogen when it greens up. With my well, I will water wheat three times if the season is normal: once at green-up, once at jointing, and once around grain filling. For maize, I will move fast after wheat harvest so I do not lose moisture and time. I will use hybrid maize seed, because around here the hybrids fill better and stand better than old seed. I will keep fertilizer a little on the safe side, because losing maize yield costs more than a bit of extra fertilizer. I will spray when I see real pressure, but I will still plan two pesticide rounds for each crop in a normal year. I will keep costs in mind because 8 mu is not big, family money must stretch, and fertilizer, pesticide, and irrigation all come from the same pocket.
